response.sql:
WITH side_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    o.dealedge,
    COUNT(*) as side_count
  FROM orders o
  INNER JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.dealedge
),
avg_count_cte AS (
  SELECT AVG(side_count) as avg_count FROM side_counts
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    side_count,
    side_count - (SELECT avg_count FROM avg_count_cte) as excess
  FROM side_counts
  WHERE side_count > (SELECT avg_count FROM avg_count_cte)
)
SELECT 
  SUM(side_count) as total_count,
  SUM(excess) / COUNT(*) as avg_excess
FROM above_avg;

assumptions.assumption: Counting riskandmargin join rows (not distinct orders). If multiple risk/margin records reference the same order, each is counted separately in the side totals.
Dealedge values define the 'sides'. If no side exceeds the average count, the result set is empty.

alternatives.interpretation: Count distinct orders per side instead of risk/margin join rows. Each order is counted once per side, even if multiple risk records match it.
alternatives.sql:
WITH side_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    o.dealedge,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) as side_count
  FROM orders o
  INNER JOIN riskandmargin r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.dealedge
),
avg_count_cte AS (
  SELECT AVG(side_count) as avg_count FROM side_counts
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    side_count,
    side_count - (SELECT avg_count FROM avg_count_cte) as excess
  FROM side_counts
  WHERE side_count > (SELECT avg_count FROM avg_count_cte)
)
SELECT 
  SUM(side_count) as total_count,
  SUM(excess) / COUNT(*) as avg_excess
FROM above_avg;
